title: Stage 10 — Frontend Application
goal: Turn the web folder into a multi-view app with login, auth gates, role-aware UI, and search — vanilla JavaScript only.
summary: No React. Navigation, auth screens, and search wired to the API you proved in Postman.

checkpoint.prompt: Vanilla JS multi-view app: user clicks "Settings". Simplest navigation pattern?

choices.text: Hide all sections, show the settings section (or update hash route)
Reload the entire page from the server for every click
Install React Router

checkpoint.explanation: Track 1 uses show/hide sections or hash routes — no framework router required.

checkpoint.prompt: After login, where should the frontend keep the access token for fetch calls?

choices.text: Memory or localStorage — sent as Authorization Bearer header
In the URL query string on every page
Hardcoded in index.html

checkpoint.explanation: Bearer tokens in memory or localStorage match the JWT API from Stage 9. Never expose tokens in URLs.

checkpoint.prompt: User opens /app without a valid token. What should the client do?

choices.text: Show login view — don't render protected content
Show the app anyway; API will error later
Delete the database

checkpoint.explanation: Auth gate runs before protected views. Call GET /me or check stored token on app boot.

checkpoint.prompt: User role is `user`, not `admin`. Delete-user button should…

choices.text: Not render in the DOM — UI hides what they can't do
Always show — security is only the API's job
Show but disable CSS only

checkpoint.explanation: API enforces 403, but good UX hides actions the user cannot perform. Check role from /me.

checkpoint.prompt: Search box calls GET /workouts?q=run. Best first approach to avoid spamming the API?

choices.text: Search on form submit or debounce input (~300ms)
fetch on every keypress with zero delay
Never call the API — filter only client-side mock data

checkpoint.explanation: Submit or debounce keeps requests reasonable. Wire to the paginated search API from Stage 7.

checklist.label: App shell with navigation between list, detail/form, and settings views
Login and register forms call API and store tokens
Unauthenticated users see login — not the main app
Admin-only controls hidden unless role is admin
Search input calls API with ?q= and shows results
Logout clears tokens and returns to login view

questions.prompt: Vanilla JS multi-view navigation without React typically uses…

choices.text: Show/hide DOM sections or hash-based routes (#/list)
JSX components only
A separate HTML file per button click with full server round-trip required

questions.explanation: Single-page feel is achievable with plain DOM manipulation or hash routing.

questions.prompt: Authenticated fetch to GET /me should include…

choices.text: Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>
The password in the JSON body
No headers — cookies are always automatic

questions.explanation: Stage 9 issued JWTs. The frontend sends the access token on protected requests.

questions.prompt: An auth gate on app startup prevents…

choices.text: Showing protected UI before verifying the user is logged in
The API from running
Users from ever registering

questions.explanation: Check token or call /me before rendering the app shell.

questions.prompt: Why hide admin buttons when role !== admin if the API already returns 403?

choices.text: Better UX — don't show actions that will fail
API 403 is optional; UI is the only security layer
Admin buttons must always be visible for debugging

questions.explanation: API enforces security. UI reflects permissions so users aren't confused.

questions.prompt: Search box wired to GET /workouts?q=term should…

choices.text: Replace or update the list with API results for that query
Only filter items already loaded on page 1 forever
POST the search term to /auth/login

questions.explanation: Search hits the server-side filter from Stage 7. Re-render the list from the response.
